meta.description: Module 4 — Proposal assembly (pure module). Entry: Execute Workflow Trigger receiving { client_id, client_config?, email_context?, data:{ rfq, content, pricing? } }. Renders the client's .docx MASTER template (selected by language) with docxtemplater: real Word headings, native bullet lists and a price table, with out-of-scope chapters dropped whole via {#has_*} blocks. Converts to PDF through Gotenberg, files the .docx in the client's Drive folder, then REPLIES IN-THREAD to the client's OWN commercial contact (never the extracted end customer) from the client's verified send-as alias, attaching both files, and sends a Telegram alert. Delivery is create-draft -> drafts.send because the Gmail node's Send operation would overwrite From with the authenticated address; client_config.send_mode='draft' stops at the draft. Template authoring: docs/TEMPLATE-GUIDE.md. Schema: schemas/proposal-assembly.schema.json.

nodes.name: Download Template
nodes.notes: template_id now points at a .docx FILE in Drive, not a Google Doc. No conversion option: we want the raw .docx bytes so the client's styles, headers and logos survive untouched.

nodes.name: Render Docx
nodes.notes: Community node n8n-nodes-docxtemplater (install via Settings > Community Nodes). Paragraph Loop MUST stay on — it is what lets {#has_x} on its own line delete the whole chapter, heading included, and what turns a loop into real list items instead of one run-on paragraph. Caveats: the node exposes no nullGetter, so a tag with no key renders the literal "undefined" (Compute Proposal Fields therefore emits every key, always); and it parses tags with Jexl, so key names must avoid "-" and loops must iterate objects, not bare strings. NOTE: this node outputs a fresh item (json: {}, only its own binary) — nothing upstream survives it.

nodes.name: Convert To PDF
nodes.notes: Gotenberg (LibreOffice) renders the .docx to PDF with the layout intact. The URL is the docker-compose service name — change it here if yours differs (see docs/DEPLOYMENT.md). The multipart field MUST be named "files", and Gotenberg picks the converter from the uploaded file's extension, which is why Render Docx names the output *.docx.

parameters.content:
## Module 4 — Proposal assembly (.docx, scope-aware, delivered)
Entry: **Execute Workflow Trigger** receiving `{ client_id, client_config?, email_context?, data:{ rfq, content, pricing? } }`.

**Compute Proposal Fields** applies the legacy fixes (G1 recipient, G2 language template, B2 deterministic number, B1 quantity) and builds a **structured render context** — mirrored from `modules/proposal/render_context.js`, checkable offline with `node modules/proposal/render_context.js`. It no longer emits pre-formatted text: headings, bullets and the price table are *structure*, and structure cannot travel through a text placeholder, which is why the Google Docs find-and-replace pipeline is gone.

**Download Template → Render Docx → Upload Docx To Drive → Convert To PDF → Collect Artifacts.** The template is the client's own **.docx** (`template_id_en`/`_es` now point at a Word file, not a Google Doc), so their styles, headers and logos survive untouched. Out-of-scope chapters vanish whole — heading included — via `{#has_*}` blocks. Both the editable .docx and the PDF are attached to the reply.

⚠️ Requires the community node **n8n-nodes-docxtemplater** and a reachable **Gotenberg** service. Template authoring: **docs/TEMPLATE-GUIDE.md**.

**Delivery.** **Create Draft** (with `fromAlias` + `threadId`) → **Send Mode?** → **Send Draft** (HTTP `drafts.send`). The draft+send pair exists because the Gmail node's Send operation rebuilds `From` from the authenticated mailbox and would discard the alias. `client_config.send_mode='draft'` skips the send — the per-client rollback.
